state.goal: Fix a supported workflow example without weakening its correlation assertion or production permissions.

verified.source: A mutation creates Appointment.source=operation.id and has no business return. Its table observation is count(Appointment as visit where visit.source==operation.id), expected 1; other rows require exact rule_failed/forbidden and no writes.
verified.language: operation.id/source are production request context facts. Examples have separate row scopes, normal canonical invocation, read-only authorized observations. Documentation mentions deterministic operation identities but only explicitly names result and fixture observations, not operation in observations.
verified.implementation: Resolver intentionally omits operation from example context; type pass records Error on this member; emission yields two refusals. Native example runtime generates canonical operation_id but discards it after call. A per-row WeakMap and existing bindings proxy can retain a frozen context only for post-success table observation. Existing caller-authorized query/readonly snapshot fence remains unchanged. No new carrier or testkit API needed if canonical hooks share a private map with runner.
verified.limits: Table rows make one call. Sequence steps and failed rows must not inherit previous operation metadata; expected cells and fixture setup must not see a future operation. For successful read-only invocations there is no mutation operation id and observation access should fail explicitly.

alternatives.retain_context: Specify operation in successful mutation table observations as the actual completed request id and source, read-only, row-isolated and available only after success. Preserve source assertion unchanged. Implement checked resolver scope + private canonical-request snapshot; no grants or writable inspection, no user binding overrides. Expected values/setup cannot access it. Reads and sequences without this defined scope fail rather than inventing identity.
alternatives.rewrite_example: Keep operation unavailable in example observations. Change this example to inspect count(Appointment) under its fresh isolated row with no Appointment seeds, or add an authored source marker/result so correlation is observable without new context. Preserve success/rejection checks, but plain count would no longer check actual source=request-id assignment; adding a result changes public operation API.

repair.instructions: For a table whose mutation writes its request id into source and whose observation filters by that id, should the language admit read-only completed-call operation context in successful observations or require a rewritten example? Evaluate both stated options under the same preservation constraints.
